title: Water Cycle Basics
summary: This lesson explores how water moves above and below the Earth's surface through the continuous process of the water cycle. Students will learn about evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection using descriptive visual scenarios.

sections.text: Scene: A diagram on a light blue background illustrates water moving above and below the Earth's surface. Arrows trace a continuous path from oceans up into the sky and back down to the land. I wonder...? How does water move above and below the Earth surface? Answer: The water cycle describes how water moves above and below the Earth surface.

Scene: A bright yellow sun shines down on liquid water, turning it into vapor that rises upward. High in the cold sky, the vapor cools to form fluffy white clouds. I wonder...? What turns liquid water into vapor? Answer: Evaporation turns liquid water into vapor using heat from the sun. Condensation forms clouds when vapor cools high in the sky.

Scene: Heavy clouds release rain and snow down toward the ground below. On the surface, runoff flows into rivers, lakes, and oceans where it gathers. I wonder...? How does water return to the surface? Answer: Precipitation returns water as rain or snow. Collection gathers runoff into rivers, lakes and oceans.
